newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close modestly lower on rate hikes.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close modestly lower on rate hikes.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed mildly lower on Friday in a muted response to the central bank's hiking of two rates, indicating a market belief that the tightening was more symbolic than substantial, brokers said.
Taking a breather from its volatile bull charge of recent weeks, the weighted index traded in a narrow range for most of the session but managed -- just barely -- to stay above 10,000 at the close.
The index finished at 10,001.56, down 0.64 percent or 64.79 points.
Turnover also was moderate at T$189.61 billion.

The central bank late on Thursday announced a modest tightening of monetary policy by raising the rediscount rate to 5.25 percent from 5.00 and accommodations against secured loans to 5.625 percent from 5.375, effective from Friday.

Bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said there was a consensus that the stock market may be slightly overheated with its torrential recent turnover, but said the bank had no opinion on whether the current index level was too high.
"You could call today a courtesy fall after the central bank's move," said United Securities analyst Lin Long-hsien.
"The two rates that the central bank hiked have mostly symbolic usage, and by raising them the central bank is sending out a message without actually changing any substantial policies," Lin said.
Constructions and financials fell 2.30 percent and 1.51 percent respectively on jitters over potentially higher capital requirements for investments due to the rate hikes.

Recent rally bellwether electronics, which analysts say have replaced financials as Taiwan's economic bedrock, finished 0.23 percent higher on continued expectations of surging sales orders through 1997.
